text: THE READING ROOM公開コード・データ / Public code and data Particle methods and smoothed particle hydrodynamics Lagrangian particles carry quantities while moving with a flow. SPH replaces a field value or derivative by a local kernel-weighted particle sum. The independent early papers by Gingold and Monaghan (1977) and Lucy (1977) are historical starting points. The static reconstruction below does not reproduce their stellar calculations. From an integral to particles# A smoothed field is approximated by fh(x)=∫f(x′)W(x−x′,h) dx′≈∑bmbρbfbW(x−xb,h).fh​(x)=∫f(x′)W(x−x′,h)dx′≈b∑​ρb​mb​​fb​W(x−xb​,h). The volume weight m_b/rho_b matters. Smoothing length h is a kernel scale, not necessarily the particle spacing. Compact support defines the neighbor search; it does not impose a fixed mesh connectivity. Our one-dimensional example uses the normalized cubic spline, with q = |x|/h: W(x,h)=23h{1−32q2+34q3,0≤q<1,14(2−q)3,1≤q<2,0,q≥2.W(x,h)=3h2​⎩⎨⎧​1−23​q2+43​q3,41​(2−q)3,0,​0≤q<1,1≤q<2,q≥2.​ This prefactor is one-dimensional. Two- and three-dimensional kernels require different normalization constants. Partition of unity and correction# The raw sum of particle volumes times W need not equal one on a discrete particle set. A Shepard-normalized interpolant divides by that sum. It reproduces a constant wherever the denominator is nonzero, but this interpolation correction alone does not establish conservative dynamics, linear consistency, or stable pressure forces. import numpy as np from numart.geometry import sph_reconstruct p = (np.arange(64) + 0.5) / 64 x = np.linspace(0, 1, 201) f, partition = sph_reconstruct(x, p, np.sin(2*np.pi*p), h=0.04) f_corrected, _ = sph_reconstruct(x, p, np.sin(2*np.pi*p), h=0.04, normalize=True) The routine uses periodic minimum-image distances on [0,1] and equal volume weights 1/N. It requires 0 < h < 1/4 so the support fits the minimum-image convention. It does not infer physical density from arbitrary unequal particle spacings. What a fluid solver would additionally need# Density estimation or a continuity update, a consistent pressure force, momentum and energy evolution, boundary particles, time stepping, neighbor-search updates, and treatment of shocks or tensile/pairing instabilities are additional modeling decisions. Artificial viscosity used in shock-capturing SPH must be distinguished from the physical Newtonian viscous stress tensor. Tests check the continuous kernel’s normalization and discrete constant reproduction after normalization. This edition implements kernel reconstruction only, not an SPH flow solver. See time integration for why a particle kick–drift leapfrog and a two-step first-order ODE leapfrog should not be conflated. Particle gravity is a separate operator# PM, P³M, Tree, and multipole methods compute gravitational fields; SPH kernels reconstruct fluid quantities and their derivatives. Read particle gravity, isolated and slab boundary kernels, and symplectic time integration to connect these different parts of a self-gravitating particle model. Godunov SPH: the Riemann-solver branch# Inutsuka's GSPH connects particle hydrodynamics with pairwise Riemann problems. The chapter follows the 2002 convolution-based derivation, identifies its 1994 precursor, and links the 2011 MHD extension by Iwasaki and Inutsuka.
